speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I see you are suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to understand the underlying cause, please tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if you smoke or have been exposed to secondhand smoke.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very long duration for recurrent bronchitis, and the description of "thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum" is particularly interesting. Given your history of multiple evaluations for bronchiectasis-like symptoms, have you ever had a high-resolution CT scan of your chest or a sputum culture to identify any specific pathogens like *Pseudomonas*?

REQUEST TEST: High_Resolution_CT_Chest
REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The history of chronic productive cough with purulent sputum, morning worsening, and recurrent "bronchitis" in a non-smoker is classic for this condition; the requested HRCT and sputum culture will confirm the diagnosis and identify pathogens.
